goals: Assemble Pariah and Anti-Venom and protect them
primary_plan: assemble a pair: any creature that cannot die, carrying any damage-redirection effect
damage-proof hosts are redundant — Anti-Venom, Horrifying Healer; Cho-Manno, Revolutionary; Phyrexian Vindicator. Any of them works.
redirection effects are redundant too — Pariah; Pariah's Shield; With Great Power . . . Any of them works.
once the pair is live you take no damage and are effectively immortal; protect the pair
win from behind it — commander damage, or redirect damage into an opponent via Stuffy Doll

Assemble any damage-proof creature with any damage-redirection effect, then use damage-based removal and combat to make the pairing control the board. Anti-Venom is one host, not the only required host; protect the two-card engine from exile, bounce, and sacrifice effects.

hard_rules: The plan is a PAIR, not two specific cards. Any damage-proof creature plus any Pariah effect is good enough — do not hold a redirection effect waiting for one particular host, and do not treat losing one host as losing the plan. Both halves are redundant by design.

CORRECTION to the auto-generated combo_lines above: Stuffy Doll + Pariah is NOT a draw. It instantly kills one opponent, then the loop ends because that opponent is dead. Treat it as a kill line, not a game-ending loop to avoid.
If a damage-proof host is already on the battlefield and a redirection effect is castable or equippable, completing the pair is urgent — that is the turn the deck stops losing.
Removal aimed at the assembled pair is the highest threat on the board. Removal aimed at a spare host or spare redirection effect is not — those are replaceable.

Pilot's rule: a Pariah effect goes on an opponent's creature only when severely on the back foot and the own pair cannot be assembled. With a damage-proof host available, always assemble the pair instead.
